spans.text: Rott is a false deity - a contorted yokai - that seeks to consume the world and draw it into the Realm of Shadows. Deep in the pits of the Realm of Shadow’s mists, the tree-like undead behemoth lays dormant, extending its will outward into the Prime Material Plane. It is a direct enemy of Aymere, who it sees as its antithesis. Rott is incapable of fully emerging in the Prime Material Plane due to its absurd size, and for fear of Aymere directly intervening and killing it. The beast presently has its true location hidden from its would-be rival, and it prefers to keep it that way. Instead, Rott infects the world by sending its seeds to infest communities. Most are found and stopped by Aymere, but occasionally one will get by, and begin to sprout into a Tree of Loathsome Nightmares, which seems to seize a community and convert them into infested undead. If successful, it will create a Seed of Rott within the tree and give birth to an avatar from a willing host, who makes it their mission to further feed the tree and create an undead horde for it.

Rott has many necromantic followers who seek eternal life through it. Some willingly give themselves to the tree in hopes of becoming one of its avatars, while others try to reproduce its undead attributes through necromancy, aiming to create a facsimile for an avatar, known as a grave lily. This persistent but growing religion has one particular goal passed down to them by Rott: find the primal gemstone of Aymere, and seal its powers away, both to be used by Rott to grow and to prevent Aymere from manifesting in the Material Plane. If such a feat were properly completed, Rott would have nothing to fear from the Wise Forest if it manifested in the Material Plane.

Hivemind. The mind of a seed or avatar of Rott is connected to all other creatures controlled by Rott, as well as Rott itself. Its god becomes aware of everything it perceives through its senses and those connected to it, and the seed perceives everything all of Rott’s servants within 500 feet of it perceives.

“So many forces in Somnus Domina erode mankind into something lesser. The mortal mind is something desirable to creatures without a concept of mortality, likely because we live our lives with a fear of death and, as a result, a love of life they cannot imagine. It is a pity they seek to take that from us rather than nurture it.”
